The statement needs substantial rewriting, and I'm working on it.

There are currently too few cases. The cases should follow the order in which the rules are presented in the statement, starting with simple cases and progressively introducing the trickier interactions. Each new rule should ideally have a simple case that demonstrates it in isolation before it's combined with other rules. Example:

* Pair 1: Simple flooding: A basic case where the water reaches the flooding row and spreads in all four directions. Test 1 should be modified so that the "o" is in the middle of the grid, with a few additional rows below the flooding row to demonstrate the extent of the flood.

* Pair 2: Simple falling without flooding: Same setup as Pair 1, but set r to the bottom row (a flat surface).

In the pairs below, flooding does not necessarily need to spread in all directions as in the current Test 1.

* Pair 3: Flood level above cell (currently Pair 5)

* Pair 4: Spread and split (_ and ^)

* Pair 5: Walls (| and #)

* Pair 6: Slopes (\ and /)

* Pair 7: Multiple "o" (currently Pair 4)

* Pair 8: Obstructions and blocked branches

* Other pairs as required

* Tricky terrain (currently Pair 3)

* A few pairs of comprehensive cases

Overall, the cases should serve as a progression through the statement.

Once I've finished the rest of the review, I'll get back to you. In the meantime, please rework the cases along these lines first. Thank you.

Sure, please take your time.

I think the concept is good, and there's definitely a good programming problem here.

As for the English, wording/grammar issues do exist, but they aren't the biggest concern. The more important thing is to make sure the rules themselves are precise and easy to follow, especially given that some aspects are currently missing. No worries, I'll take care of the statement for you 😉
Update: right now the only pairs missing are pair 4, pair 8 and comprehensive cases. I'll add them later im just going to take a break. also can you explain what are comprehensive cases?

By "comprehensive cases", I mean cases that combine several of the rules introduced earlier, to make sure the overall behaviour is correct. They're more complex scenarios involving things like multiple terrain types, multiple water-generating cells, flooding, blocked branches, etc.

Below is the revised statement. It's a draft and subject to further updates. Could you please take a look and see if my understanding is correct?

Here at Water-Generating Cells™ Corporation, we sell cells that generate water to our clients and fill whatever holes they have so they can make lakes, pools, miniature waterfalls, and similar features, with ease. We are trying to offer an experience where the client can see what their body of water would look like before we deliver and apply the cells. That's where you come in.

You will be given the dimensions and the 2-dimensional ASCII representation of the client's area, which contains at least one water-generating cell {{o}}. It generates a water stream {{~}} (tilde) that initially only goes downward, but will stop and start flooding at row [[r]] (0-based).

<<Terrains>>

When a falling stream encounters a cell, its behavior depends on the character in that cell:

{{.}} is an empty space. The stream enters it and continues downward.

{{_}} is a flat terrain. The stream spreads in two directions, left and right, on the row immediately above the terrain. In each direction, the stream continues spreading until it can continue downward again, or until the path is blocked.

{{^}} is a sharp terrain. The stream splits into two branches, which enters the cells immediately to the left and right of the terrain. Both branches then continue downward. A branch is created only if the destination cell is empty.

{{|}} is a thin wall. It results in the same two-way split as {{^}}. An exception is that when either or both branches are blocked, the wall becomes waterlogged ({{!}}), and the stream continues downward in the unblocked branch (if any) as well as through the wall.

{{#}} is a thick wall. The stream simply stops.

{{\}} and {{/}} are slopes. The stream moves to the cell immediately left of {{/}} and immediately right of {{\}} before continuing downward.

<<Obstructions>>

{{.}} is the only ordinary cell that a stream can enter. When entered by a stream, it becomes {{~}}. A thin wall {{|}} that is waterlogged becomes {{!}} and can also be traversed by a downward stream (but does not become {{~}}).

A stream cannot enter any cell containing terrain, another stream, or a water-generating cell. The boundary of the area is also treated as an obstruction. The only exceptions are empty cells {{.}} and waterlogged thin walls {{!}}, which are handled as described above.

If a stream attempts to enter an obstructed cell, that stream ceases to exist.

<<Flooding>>

If a stream reaches row [[r]], it becomes flood water. Flood water attempts to spread to the four neighboring cells (up, down, left, right), entering only {{.}} cells. Flooding is limited to row [[r]] and below; flood water cannot spread above row [[r]].

<<Task>>

Your task is to output the final state of the client's area after all streams have been generated by the water-generating cells and have interacted with the various features in the area.

You did a really great work refining the statement, though there are a few things I intended to put that I didn't see there.
- In order for the sharp terrain or the thin wall to split the stream, the cells to the left and right of it and the ones directly above those must be unobstructed.
- The waterlogged thin wall will waterlog other thin walls beneath it, without splitting the stream.
- It might be good to specify that the thin wall does not waterlog inside flood water.
I'll apply the changes as needed, thank you!

Ah, good catch on the small details I missed earlier! Those details should definitely be showcased in the simpler cases, and also later in the comprehensive cases.

* Consider changing as follows:

  • Replace the first paragraph with:

Here at Water-Generating Cells™ Corporation, we sell cells that generate water for our clients. These cells can fill any suitable area, allowing our clients to create lakes, pools, miniature waterfalls, and similar features with ease. We want our clients to be able to preview what their body of water will look like before we deliver and install the cells. That's where you come in.

  • will be given => are given

  • will stop and start => starts

  • Terrains => Terrain

  • which enters => which enter

  • the destination cell is empty, as well as the one directly above it => both its destination cell and the cell directly above it are empty

  • In case there is another thin wall beneath, that one will only be waterlogged and the stream will not split. => If another thin wall is directly below a waterlogged thin wall, that wall also becomes waterlogged but does not split the stream.

  • becomes flood water => becomes flood water, also represented by {{~}}

* Please add "and through the wall" after "unblocked branch (if any)", as this refers to the fact that the stream appears directly below "!" when there is no obstruction.

* I think we should specify what happens (under the Obstructions section) when two streams or water cells merge, e.g.

If two {{~}} attempt to enter the same {{.}} cell, both succeed and merge into a single {{~}}.

* It seems a bit unintuitive to me that thin walls do not become waterlogged when inside flood water. I'm not saying that you necessarily need to change the design, but perhaps it's worth giving some thought.

Input
* Please change:
  • The [[w]]idth => An integer [[w]] for the width
  • The [[h]]idth => An integer [[h]] for the height
  • The [[r]]ow => An integer [[r]] for the row
  • for each line => in each line

Constraints
* Please change the lower bounds of [[w]] and [[h]] to 1.

* Please change "<= [[h]] - 1" to "< [[h]]".

* Is it correct to add a constraint specifying that the client's area never contains any waterlogged thin walls ({{!}}) initially? Or should cases which include ! in the initial state be added instead?

Stub generator
* Please change 256 to 30.

Cases
* Please rename the case "Multipler Cells", as "multipler" isn't a valid English word.

There may be more points that need clarification, but let's proceed with the ones above and the case creation first.

Thanks.

Hello, I added the changes. It makes sense for the thin wall to be waterlogged in the flood water, so I changed the statement to say:
- Thin walls {{|}} are only waterlogged inside flood water when it's surrounded by water in at least 3 cardinal directions.
